requirement:
`habeas add-input --item <file>:<line>` MUST parse the file under {cite}`requirements.references.outlines` and add or refresh one
outline input for every outline node declared on that line. A named node is
declared on the line containing its name; an anonymous node is declared on the
line where it starts. Each input MUST store the selected `file` under the path
rules in {cite}`requirements.ci.schema`, the node's selector, and its structural
hash. The command MUST report every selected node and reject a line on which no
node is declared.
rationale:
**Judgment:** the implementation is complete and tested. I am marking the requirement as satisfied.

**Implementation**
- **CLI:** `src/main.rs` (`Command::AddInput` and `main`) defines `add-input --item <file:line>`. clap requires exactly one target and exactly one mode, and the command calls `habeas::add_input`.
- **Parsing:** `selectors_for_mode` in `src/add_input.rs` splits the argument at the last `:` and parses the line number. It parses the file through `OutlineCache::parse`, which uses the outline profiles from `requirements.references.outlines`. Parse errors and missing files are returned as errors.
- **Selecting nodes:** `Outline::declared_on_line` in `src/outline/mod.rs` returns every non-root node whose `declaration_line` equals the requested line.
  - `Builder::name` and `Builder::walk` set that line to the name's start byte for named nodes, and to the node's start byte for anonymous ones.
  - `Builder::finish` copies it into `declaration_line` via `lines.line(draft.declaration_byte)`.
  - `plain_text` makes each non-blank line an anonymous `line` node declared on its own line.
  - Together these match "a named node is declared on the line containing its name; an anonymous node is declared on the line where it starts".
- **Rejection:** if no node is declared on the line, `selectors_for_mode` returns `"{file}:{line}: no outline node is declared on this line"`.
- **Stored input:** `InputSelector::to_input` (`src/inputs.rs`) stores `file`, `item` (the node's selector) and `hash` (the structural hash). It stores no source text. `resolve` computes the hash.
- **Path rules:** `selectors_for_mode` strips the project root from the file path, so project files are stored relative to it. Permitted external paths stay absolute, as `requirements.ci.schema` allows.
- **Add or refresh:** `update_inputs` finds an existing input with the same selector. It then reports `unchanged`, `refreshed` or `added`, and each report line names the selector.
- **Reporting:** `update_inputs` writes one report line per selected node, so every selected node is reported.
- **Other behavior in the marked code:** the review reset and definition capture in `update_inputs` belong to `cli.add_input` and `definitions.capture`, which that function also marks.
- **Marking:** all code that implements the requirement carries `{impl}` markers. Examples are `declared_on_line`, `plain_text`, `name`, `walk` and `finish`.

**Tests** (`tests/commands.rs`, plus `src/outline/tests.rs::line_queries_find_innermost_and_declared_nodes`)
- `add_input_modes_capture_outline_nodes_and_refresh_idempotently`:
  - Line 4 of a Rust file has a doc comment and an attribute above a function that contains a nested function. Both `fn[main]` and `fn[main]/fn[nested]` are added and reported.
  - A plain-text line is added as an anonymous `line@…` node.
  - A repeated add reports `unchanged` and leaves the file byte-identical.
  - Rejected locations leave the record untouched: a line with no declared node (`src/main.rs:3`, with the exact message), a blank line (`notes.txt:2`), a non-numeric line (`src/main.rs:x`) and a missing file (`missing.rs:1`).
  - The stored hash ignores citation comment edits but changes when the doc comment changes, which confirms the structural hash is what is stored.
- `add_input_requires_one_target_and_mode_and_resets_changed_records`:
  - clap rejects invalid target and mode combinations.
  - Unchanged inputs are reported as `unchanged`.
  - Changed sources are refreshed in place with a `refreshed` report.
- `add_input_external_sources_respect_allow_and_disallow` covers an external absolute file path that is allowed, which stores the absolute path. It also covers a disallowed one, which is rejected and leaves the record unchanged.
- `line_queries_find_innermost_and_declared_nodes` tests `declared_on_line` directly. Two nodes declared on one line are returned together (`impl[Thing]` and `impl[Thing]/fn[run]`).

**Minor point:** I found no test of a named node whose name sits on a later line than its start. The doc-comment and attribute case covers the main difference between the declaration line and the node's start line. This does not change my judgment.

text: :::{req} add_input_item
`habeas add-input --item <file>:<line>` MUST parse the file under {cite}`requirements.references.outlines` and add or refresh one
outline input for every outline node declared on that line. A named node is
declared on the line containing its name; an anonymous node is declared on the
line where it starts. Each input MUST store the selected `file` under the path
rules in {cite}`requirements.ci.schema`, the node's selector, and its structural
hash. The command MUST report every selected node and reject a line on which no
node is declared.
:::{req} outlines
Habeas MUST parse Rust, Python, TypeScript, CSS, Markdown, TOML, and YAML
sources with pinned tree-sitter grammars, selected by file extension compared
case-insensitively. A source with any syntax error MUST fail to parse, reporting
the line of its first error. Every
other text file MUST use a plain-text profile in which each line that is not
blank is an anonymous outline node of kind `line`. Each supported language MUST
have an outline profile that maps grammar node kinds to short outline kind names
and, for each mapped kind, states whether a node is named, and by which fields
or children, or anonymous. Only mapped kinds MUST appear in the outline; other
nodes MUST be transparent, so their outline descendants appear under the
nearest outline ancestor. A profile MAY attach grammar siblings to an outline
node, such as Rust attributes and doc comments preceding an item, so the outline
tree need not match the grammar tree exactly; attached siblings are part of that
node for its line range and hash. Every file's outline MUST have a root node
for the whole file, independent of language. Source in no other outline node,
such as top-level statements no profile maps, MUST belong to the root node;
profiles MUST NOT invent fallback kinds for it. Comments MUST NOT be outline nodes. Profiles MUST be
documented. Upgrading a grammar or profile MAY change outlines and MUST be
treated as a deliberate change.
:::{req} schema

A requirement or example evidence file at `evidence/<full-name>.json` MUST be a JSON object with exactly `requirement` or `example`, `determination`, `rationale`, and `inputs`. The definition text and rationale MUST be nonempty strings, `determination` MUST use one of the outcomes defined by {cite}`requirements.ci.outcomes`, and `inputs` MUST be an array. Every evidence input MUST have exactly one of three forms: an outline input with `file`, `item`, and `hash`; a requirements input with `requirements`, `matches`, and `text`; or a definition input with `definition` and `text`. File paths MUST resolve to permitted inputs under {cite}`requirements.ci.input_containment`. Project-local paths SHOULD be recorded relative to the project for portability; absolute and parent-relative paths MAY be used when their resolved targets are permitted. `matches` MUST be an array of distinct full definition names, `hash` MUST be a lowercase hexadecimal SHA-256 digest, and `text` MUST be a nonempty array of strings. Evidence MUST NOT store source text for outline inputs.
